EXISTENCE OF VISCOSITY SOLUTIONS WITH THE OPTIMAL
REGULARITY OF A TWO-PEAKON HAMILTON–JACOBI EQUATION
TOMASZ CIEŚLAK AND JAKUB SIEMIANOWSKI
Abstract. This work, which continues the research begun in [6], [7], is devoted to the studies of
a Hamilton–Jacobi equation with a quadratic and degenerate Hamiltonian, which comes from the
dynamics of a multipeakon in the Camassa–Holm equation. It is given by a quadratic form with a
singular positive semi-deﬁnite matrix. We increase the regularity of the value function considered
in [6], which is known to be the viscosity solution. We prove that for a two-peakon Hamiltonian
such solutions are actually 1/2-Hölder continuous in space and time-Lipschitz continuous.
The
time-Lipschitz regularity is proven in any dimension N ≥1. Such a regularity is already known in
the one-dimensional simpliﬁcations (see [7]), moreover it is the best possible, as shown in [6, 7].

Such a problem arises in the investigation of dynamics of a two-peakon special solutions to the
Camassa–Holm equation, see for instance [2, 3].
The multipeakon is a solution of the form u(x, t) = PN
i=1 pi(t)e−|x−qi(t)|, which satisﬁes Camassa–
Holm equation provided pi, qi are trajectories of the Hamiltonian system with the Hamiltonian
given by the quadratic form H(q, p) := 1/2E(q)p · p, p = (p1, p2, . . . , pN), q = (q1, q2, . . . , qN). The
evolution of a multipeakon was an area of many investigations during last years, besides already
mentioned [2, 3], see for instance [5, 13], where geometric tools are used to trace the dynamics of
multipeakon. Further information can be found in the introductory part of [6]. The Hamilton–
Jacobi equation is a natural description of the front propagation of multipeakon trajectories. This
is an original source of our interest in (1.1). Our study continues our previous contribution in [6, 7].
Let us mention that (1.1) seems additionally interesting since, due to its degeneracy, it is not covered
by the classical theory of unique solvability of the Hamilton–Jacobi equation.
Neither classical
approach of viscosity solutions (see [8, 10]) nor viability theory methods (see [11, 12]) seem directly
applicable in this case. The matrix E(x), x = (x1, x2, . . . , xN), becomes singular once xi = xj for
i ̸= j but it is positive semi-deﬁnite, see [5] for a proof of this fact (when xi ̸= xj for i ̸= j, matrix
E(x) is even positive deﬁnite). Due to the symmetry and positive semi-deﬁniteness of E(x), the

We show that the value function which is a visocsity solution to the Hamilton–Jacobi equation with
the two-peakon Hamiltonian, constructed in [6], is 1/2-Hölder continuous in space and time-Lipschitz
continuous. This is the best possible regularity. We know from [7] that even in the one-dimensional
simpliﬁcation higher regularity fails, see also [6, Proposition 5.4] for the explicit example. Last but
not least, we show that time-Lipschitz continuity of a solution of (1.1), constructed in [6], holds
in any dimension N ≥1, see Theorem 3 in Section 3. It is worth mentioning that the optimal
regularity obtained in this paper is still not enough to prove the uniqueness of a viscosity solution.
Actually, quite a standard use of a doubling variables method, yields global uniqueness provided
solutions are (1/2 + ǫ)-Hölder continuous in the space variable. For more information on this issue
as well as more sophisticated local-in-time uniqueness, we refer to [6, Section 5].
Our main theorem reads.
Theorem 1. Let N = 2 and g be bounded and Lipschitz continuous. Then a bounded viscosity
solution u of (1.1), constructed in [6], admits the following regularity: there is C > 0 such that for
all (y, t), (˜y, ˜t) ∈R2 × [0, T]

3. Regularity
In this section we show that the value function v deﬁned by (2.3) associated with the two-dimensional
terminal-value problem (2.2) is 1/2-Hölder continuous in space and time-Lipschitz continuous. We
emphasize that the obtained regularity is the best possible. In fact, we obtain a time-Lipschitz
continuity of a value function v in any dimension N ≥1.
As a consequence of the regularity
estimates, the value function turns to be an almost everywhere diﬀerentiable viscosity solution to
initial and terminal-value problems.
Let us say a few words concerning the technical aspects. Our proof is based on an optimal control
reformulation (2.3) and estimates of the value function. To avoid repeating the similar arguments in
slightly diﬀerent circumstances, an abstract Lemma 4 is proven. This lemma is helpful in showing
the full regularity proof in the possibly shortest way. Moreover, since Lemma 4 is formulated in any
dimension N ≥1, it can be used in a future work on higher dimensional regularity.

Abstract: This work, which continues the research begun in [6], [7], is devoted to the studies of a Hamilton–Jacobi equation with a quadratic and degenerate Hamiltonian, which comes from the dynamics of a multipeakon in the Camassa–Holm equation. It is given by a quadratic form with a singular positive semi-deﬁnite matrix. We increase the regularity of the value function considered in [6], which is known to be the viscosity solution. We prove that for a two-peakon Hamiltonian such solutions are actually 1/2-Hölder continuous in space and time-Lipschitz continuous. The time-Lipschitz regularity is proven in any dimension N ≥1. Such a regularity is already known in the one-dimensional simpliﬁcations (see [7]), moreover it is the best possible, as shown in [6, 7].
